articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Offseason buzz

ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal!

Nov. 9

Hoop Collective: Are the Lakers and Warriors legit contenders in the West?

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover surprising starts for several teams in the NBA, including the rejuvenated Golden State Warriors and the impressive Los Angeles Lakers. They then break down the latest Oklahoma City Thunder trade before closing on the first matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers this season.

Topics: 

0:48: Early surprises of the NBA season

2:58: Do the Warriors need to be taken seriously?

15:36: What does Kristaps Porzingis' update mean for Warriors?

22:13: Lakers starting to look like a complete team

33:48: An interesting trade by the Thunder

49:45: First 76ers-Celtics matchup Tuesday

MacMahon on why the Thunder made the trade on Sunday: "First off, the Thunder need wings. So the the Thunder needed a wing and they needed to manage the payroll. And you know when we did the thing on the Thunder in the wake -- we didn't know at the time how long Chet was going to be out -- but in the wake of the injuries to Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams, we talked to people around the league about all the different ways that Thunder might address this.

"And we talked about how, hey, going after a guy like a Herb Jones or Trey Murphy, like don't hold your breath for the Thunder to take on a contract of those sizes because they're having to manage their payroll, which is why they traded three role players who helped them win a championship just a couple of years ago.

"This is a buy-low deal, just like it was with Jared McCain.

"... He's got this year plus two more left on his rookie contract, and next year, his salary is $3.4 million. So a year after that, it's five, five and change, like it's almost six. Look I don't know whether Nique Clifford will work out. But this is exactly the type of move that the Thunder specialize in."

articles.headline: Fantasy risers and fallers: Add Burries, give more time to struggling Buzelis?
articles.description: Steve Alexander looks at three players on the rise and three who are slumping and how fantasy managers should react.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー注目選手：バリーズを追加し、苦戦するブゼリスに時間をかけるべきか？
articles.descriptionJa: スティーブ・アレクサンダーが、上昇傾向にある3選手と低迷している3選手を挙げ、ファンタジーマネージャーがどう対応すべきかを考察します。
articles.body:
Risers and Fallers is back this week with a look at three players who are on the rise and might be worth adding, along with three others who are struggling to the point of being potential drop candidates.

I didn't write up Oklahoma City big man Aday Mara, but if you're in need of a center, Chet Holmgren is out for about three months and Mara simply has to play. I think he's going to have a big second half, and he's only rostered in 18.7% of ESPN leagues.

Fellow rookie Kingston Flemings is starting for the Atlanta Hawks and is also worth a close look, while Duncan Robinson is having a career year for the Detroit Pistons.

Here's a closer look at the latest fantasy risers and fallers around the league.

Resources: Rankings | Adds/Drops | Scoring leaders | Player Rater | Mock draft lobby | Depth charts | Schedule | Injuries

Risers

 Grayson Allen, SG/SF, Charlotte Hornets (18.3% rostered in ESPN leagues)

Allen posted a total dud Friday night, missing all five of his shots and failing to score a point in a blowout loss to the Boston Celtics. But he had 22 points, a steal, a block and five 3-pointers in his previous game, and he has scored in double figures in seven of his 10 games this season. The zero-point effort was possibly a blessing in disguise, as it means he might still be available on your waiver wire.

Allen isn't going to help you much if you're seeking steals and blocks, but he's an elite 3-point shooter, has excellent shooting percentages and can really help in scoring while also chipping in some assists and rebounds. Kon Knueppel suffered a hamstring injury in his return and will be sidelined at least four more weeks, so that provides Allen more opportunities.

 Cam Spencer, PG/SG, Memphis Grizzlies (9.4% rostered)

Ty Jerome is having an incredible season, but he has an extensive injury history and isn't likely to play in back-to-backs. And while the Grizzlies are deep in the backcourt, Spencer has emerged as their second-best point guard.

Like Allen, Spencer also put up a dud in his last game, as he hit just two of five shots for seven points and zero assists in a blowout loss Friday to the Oklahoma City Thunder. But he had seven points, six rebounds, nine assists, a steal and a 3-pointer in his previous game and is averaging 8.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 5.1 assists, 0.8 steals and 1.8 3-pointers for the season.

Those assist numbers are hard to find on the waiver wire, and while the lack of scoring is a bit annoying, Spencer could turn out to be an incredibly valuable fantasy player if Jerome goes down. And if Jerome stays healthy all season, Spencer should still be able to average around 10 points, five dimes and two 3-pointers off the bench.

 Brayden Burries, SG, Milwaukee Bucks (12.6% rostered)

Burries replaced Ryan Rollins in the starting unit for the Bucks on Nov. 2 and played well for two games, then went off for 21 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, a block and a 3-pointer in 28 minutes in Friday's loss to the Toronto Rapto

articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We already have nine deals -- and more are on the way.

With less than 48 hours until the deadline, the Jaguars made a big post-Week 9 move in trading for safety Jessie Bates III. But he isn't the only big name to get dealt so far, with Jeffery Simmons going to the Bears, J.J. McCarthy going to the Giants, Jacoby Brissett going to the Ravens and Joey Porter Jr. going to the Cowboys.

We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals will be added at the top.

More coverage:

Nov. 4

Cardinals trade QB Brissett to Ravens

Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

The Cardinals finalized a trade to send QB Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens on Friday. The Cardinals are sending a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-rounder in exchange for Brissett and a 2027 fourth-round selection.

Brissett's first start as the Ravens' starting quarterback could come as soon as Week 10 when Baltimore hosts the Chargers on "Monday Night Football." He was recently benched by the Cardinals before the trade.

Walder: Grading the deal from both sides

Hensley: Can Brissett save the Ravens?

Oct. 29

Titans trade DT Simmons to Bears

Bears get: DT Jeffery Simmons, 2028 fifth-round pick

Titans get: 2027 first-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 first-round pick

The Bears are acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Titans, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The Titans are receiving 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Bears in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the sources told Schefter.

Simmons, 29, signed a three-year, $105.8 million extension with $100 million guaranteed with the Titans in June. He is under contract through the 2030 season.

Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers

The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the team that made him a 2016 first-round pick before dealing him to Indianapolis in 2020, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Colts will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from the 49ers, sources said.

articles.headline: Rasheed Walker keeps 'analyzing issue' in protecting Bryce Young's blind side
articles.description: The left tackle can't let Sunday's sack-fumble ignite a prolonged pass protection slump over the coming weeks.
articles.headlineJa: ラシード・ウォーカー、ブライス・ヤングのブラインドサイド保護における「課題を分析中」
articles.descriptionJa: このレフトタックルは、日曜日のサック・ファンブルをきっかけに、今後数週間にわたってパスプロテクションの不振が長期化することを避けなければなりません。
articles.body:
The Panthers were 56 yards away from pay dirt and their fourth win of the season. But with just 1:24 left in the game, left tackle Rasheed Walker was pushed into the backfield by Denver Broncos pass rusher Nik Bonitto, who smacked the ball out of quarterback Bryce Young's right hand for a sack-fumble, which was recovered by the road team at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday.

The play closed out a 26-21 win for the Broncos and put Walker, who has struggled mightily with pass protection over the past month, under a microscope. Following the game, Walker said he felt like Bonitto set up that final defensive play with how he rushed Walker throughout the game.

"Bonitto is known to be a speed edge rusher -- bend the edge type of guy," Walker said. "I noticed like the whole game that he was bull-rushing me, like he doesn't really do a lot. I was sitting on the bull (rush), and then on the last play of the game, I feel like he faked the power, and then as soon as I was sitting down, he went [to the] edge and did his move and then made a play. When you're going against the best, you never know what you're going to get. Shout out to him, he's a great player and it was a good rep by him."

Walker has been charged with 45 QB pressures through eight games, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That's 19 more pressures than rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling, who has played one less game. Walker has faced one-on-one scenarios on 79.1% of his pass sets, and the free-agent addition has struggled to hold back the pressure on a consistent basis.

The 26-year-old can't let Sunday's sack-fumble ignite a prolonged pass protection slump over the coming weeks. The Panthers are in a three-game freefall at 3-5, and while they still enter Week 10 at the top of the division race, their NFC South showdown Sunday against the New Orleans Saints (3-5) looms large.

Every week Walker is typically going up against the opposing team's best pass rusher, and against the Broncos, he drew Bonitto. On that final play -- one that Walker wants back -- Bonitto beat Walker when it mattered the most.

"Just a really good rush on Rasheed," Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "Got the edge [and] was hoping that there was an element of Bryce going forward to get an incomplete pass, but a really nice rush. That's a situation where we can help him right there."

While Canales hoped the officials would signal an incomplete pass, Walker's hopes were a bit different, especially after he felt he put together a strong performance before that exclamation point for the Broncos.

"S---, when I saw the ball come out -- we both saw the ball come out, I watched him see the ball, I tried to make sure he didn't get it -- I was hoping that we got the ball back," Walker said. "I felt comfortable playing the whole game. I knew that play didn't define who I was and I was hoping that we'd get the ball back and get another opportunity to score. But, you know, they recovered the ball and that was that."

articles.headline: Early bets for Week 10: 49ers triumph in Dallas, low scoring in Texans-Browns?

articles.descriptionJa: オッズが発表された際、第10週のどのラインに即座に価値があったか？私たちが推奨する早期ベッティングを紹介します。
articles.body:
Week 9 of the NFL season wraps up with Monday night's Bills-Vikings matchup (8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN), but we're already looking ahead to Week 10. Which games grabbed our analysts' attention?

The San Francisco 49ers rebounded from their first loss of the season with a win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9 and will look to keep the momentum going Sunday on the road against the Dallas Cowboys, who narrowly defeated the Indianapolis Colts.

The Houston Texans kept the Los Angeles Chargers winless with an easy victory this past Sunday and in Week 10 will visit the Cleveland Browns, whose failed 2-point conversion near the end of overtime left them with their second straight loss.

Who do we like? Matt Bowen and Pamela Maldonado break down the games and share the bets they're backing before potential odds shifts later in the week.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures.

 San Francisco 49ers -3.5 at Dallas Cowboys

Bowen: Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas. Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road.

Last week: Bengals -3 vs. Falcons (Result:  Bengals 34-Falcons 17)

 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns UNDER 39.5

Maldonado: Neither offense runs the ball well, which puts this game on the quarterbacks. Cleveland has allowed 38 sacks. Houston's pass rush kills drives. Shedeur Sanders threw for nearly 300 yards in Week 9, but the Browns scored only 16 points in regulation. Cleveland's secondary can challenge Houston's biggest offensive strength, C.J. Stroud. I see plenty of sacks and Houston potentially controlling this game, limiting Sanders and the Browns to keep this under the total.

Last week: Cowboys-Colts OVER 52 (Result: Cowboys 27, Colts 23)

articles.headline: 'The World Cup never really ended': US-based betting sees rise in wagering on MLS, European soccer
articles.description: Before the World Cup, many wondered if Americans stick around afterwards. Betting data says yes, they did.
articles.headlineJa: 「ワールドカップは実質的に終わっていない」：米国でMLSや欧州サッカーへの賭けが増加
articles.descriptionJa: ワールドカップ前、多くの人々が大会後もアメリカ人が関心を持ち続けるか疑問視していたが、ベッティングデータによれば、その関心は持続している。
articles.body:
Soccer was the sport of the summer in the United States this year, as the FIFA World Cup came to 11 American cities (in addition to venues in Canada and Mexico). Americans embraced the sport fully, supporting tremendous numbers for television viewership and stadium attendance -- as well as sports betting handle.

BetMGM said that the World Cup "nearly kept pace with the MLB's rigorous summer schedule" despite there being five times as many baseball games over that time period. Hard Rock Bet noted the tournament did three times as much handle and brought in double the number of individual bettors as the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament, which is traditionally the most-bet on event on the U.S. sports calendar.

In Colorado, which breaks down betting revenue by sport, the World Cup generated $60.2 million, a near 250% increase from the $17.5 million brought in by the previous edition of the tournament in Nov. 2022.

With European league soccer in full swing and Major League Soccer kicking off playoffs, that momentum has continued over for the American sports betting ecosystem.

BetMGM noted that in the two-month period immediately following the conclusion of the 2026 World Cup, the sportsbook saw a 24.5% year-over-year increase in bets and a 34.5% increase in handle on wagers for club soccer. Hard Rock said there have been nearly 30% more wagers on soccer overall, specifically 43% more in the Premier League and 21% in the Champions League with World Cup stars Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Harry Kane attracting double the amount of bets in the competition compared to the same time period last year.

"The World Cup never really ended for our customers. The bettors who did well backing Mbappé, Haaland and Kane this summer have followed them straight back to the Champions League, and the post-World Cup pain continues for us every time those guys light up the scoreboard," Hard Rock Bet SVP of sportsbook Neil Walsh told ESPN over email. "Those Tuesday and Wednesday afternoon matches don't compete with primetime U.S. sports, so they get our customers' full attention."

"We have seen an immediate increase in activity across our soccer markets when comparing 2026 with 2025," Caesars lead soccer trader Mark Bickerdike said in an email.

"Encouragingly, that growth is evident across both pre-match and in-play betting and is reflected across the majority of competitions we offer. It certainly feels as though we've benefited from the momentum generated by the World Cup heading into the new domestic seasons."

MLS has attracted significantly more betting action in 2026 than it did the year prior, showing a 30.4% increase in tickets and a 38.8% increase in money from mid-July to the end of October. MLS handle is up 27% at Hard Rock Bet over a similar time period, with Inter Miami -- a fixture for the Florida-based book -- garnering almost 40% more bets year-over-year.

articles.headline: How does Jessie Bates III help the Jaguars defense? Are Falcons still contending?
articles.description: The Falcons decided it was wiser to get something for Bates now rather than letting him walk in free agency.
articles.headlineJa: ジェシー・ベイツ3世はジャガーズの守備にどう貢献するか？ファルコンズにまだ競争力はあるか？
articles.descriptionJa: ファルコンズは、ベイツをフリーエージェントで放出するよりも、今何かを得る方が賢明だと判断した。
articles.body:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars addressed one of their biggest weaknesses Monday by sending a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for safety Jessie Bates III, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

That may be just the first move the team makes before Tuesday's trade deadline to solidify itself as a legitimate contender. The Jaguars still need help at defensive tackle, especially after the loss of nose tackle DaVon Hamilton for the rest of the season with a quad injury, and the pass rush could use some help, too.

At 6-2, the Jaguars are in third place in the AFC and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. This move could suggest a win-now mentality.

Bates, who made the Pro Bowl in 2023, can stabilize a secondary that has been hit with multiple injuries at safety and cornerback. The Jaguars made a similar move last season at the trade deadline by acquiring receiver Jakobi Meyers to help a position group that had multiple players out with injuries and that keyed an offensive surge that carried them to a division title. The hope is that Bates can do the same for the secondary because getting through the AFC means beating some of the league's top QBs -- especially Buffalo's Josh Allen.

The Falcons, on the other hand, were able to get good draft capital for a player on an expiring contract but are still competing in the NFC South.

What does this move mean for the Jaguars' defense and the Falcons' draft plans? ESPN NFL Nation reporters Michael DiRocco and Marc Raimondi and NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid take a look at each.

What does the Bates addition mean for the Jaguars' defense?

The Jaguars rank second in the league in opponents points per game (15.1), yet 22nd in passing yards allowed per game (229.0).

Starting safety Eric Murray, who went on injured reserve on Nov. 3 with a season-ending elbow injury, didn't have an interception or pass breakup this season but he was valued because he was a good communicator on the field. Bates brings that, but he also has good ball skills (28 career interceptions).

Bates' durability is a huge plus, too. He has missed three games in his nine-year career while Murray has missed seven games since he signed with the Jaguars in March 2025. Murray's injury, which happened on the first play of Week 8, as well as injuries to Caleb Ransaw (placed on IR on Oct. 6 with a knee injury) and Antonio Johnson (ankle) forced the Jaguars to use special teams standout Rayuan Lane III and practice squad player Kaevon Merriweather more on defense. While both played well -- Lane made a game-saving fourth-down tackle against the Cincinnati Bengals and had a 92-yard interception return for a touchdown against the Colts -- this move gives the Jaguars a good safety tandem.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United to hire USMNT's Pochettino to replace Carrick?
articles.description: Manchester United are in the relegation zone and could turn to United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：マン・ユナイテッドがキャリックの後任に米国代表のポチェッティーノを起用か？
articles.descriptionJa: 降格圏に位置するマンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、マイケル・キャリックの後任として米国代表のマウリシオ・ポチェッティーノ監督を招聘する可能性がある。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is the current favorite to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United, while the club want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are in the relegation zone and could turn to United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick, says The Standard. In August, Pochettino, who managed Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, signed a new contract until 2030, which could complicate matters. But former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany, Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig boss Julian Nagelsmann, who are both free agents, are among the other managers also reported to be on United's shortlist.

- Football Insider reports that Man United want to bolster their defense with the signing of Nottingham Forest defender Murillo. The Brazil international, 24, joined from Corinthians in 2023 for around €6 million, but his transfer could be worth 10 times that now. United are also reported to be interested in Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri. The Red Devils were surprise suitors for the 25-year-old late in the summer, when it appeared an exit from City could be on the cards, and if they pull off a January deal it would be a rare cross-city move -- one that hasn't happened directly between the rivals since 2012.

- United have also been busy scouting other potential transfer targets in the market, according to Nicolò Schira, after attending a match between Atalanta and Monza. The club have been monitoring Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi, 26, who has a deal that expires in 2028, and Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with the 21-year-old being linked with a host of different clubs after scoring nine goals in 10 Serie A appearances.

- Fabrizio Romano has ruled out a potential move away from Inter Miami for Lionel Messi. The 39-year-old has recently been linked with a possible return to Newell's Old Boys in Argentina, one of the first teams he played for as an academy star, to see out his career. But with a contract that runs until 2028, Messi is set to stay in MLS for the next two years before considering his next possible options.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea are among a whole host of teams tracking the future of Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou, according to TEAMtalk. The 21-year-old center back has been with the French club since last summer, making 37 senior appearances in that time as he continues to develop. That has caught the eye of the two London clubs, which are looking to invest in the backline for the future, while PSG, Manchester City, Newcastle, Fulham, and Brentford are also named as clubs that have been keeping an eye on Ganiou's progress.

articles.headline: What's fueling the rocky start for Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat
articles.description: At 4-6, the Heat aren't pointing fingers -- yet. But with each loss, the pressure rises on this season and next -- with Giannis' free agency looming.
articles.headlineJa: ヤニス・アデトクンボとマイアミ・ヒートの不安定なスタートの原因とは
articles.descriptionJa: 4勝6敗という成績の中、ヒートは今のところ誰かを責めてはいない。しかし、敗戦が重なるにつれ、今シーズンと来シーズンへのプレッシャーが高まっており、ヤニスのフリーエージェントへの移行も迫っている。
articles.body:
IF THE NIGHT had ended differently, Klay Thompson would have had a very different agenda for his off day in Los Angeles. There had been talk of a visit to Catalina Island and extended visits with friends and family in his hometown.

But those plans evaporated quickly after the Miami Heat gave up a staggering 138 points in a loss to the Los Angeles Lakers last Monday.

"We need to practice," Thompson said.

It was Miami's fourth game of its first seven in which the defense had given up 125 or more points -- and it could've been worse. The Lakers had scored 79 points in the first half.

"It's important for all of us to stay present and not look too far ahead in the season," Thompson told ESPN. "When you have big expectations, you think about the postseason, you think about seeding. I think we just need to really stay week-to-week.

"That's the true joy when you build a great team. It's just the beginning stages, and then you see it jell."

Thompson would know.

The five-time All-Star won four NBA championships with the Golden State Warriors and said he still believes in what this Heat team can become just as much as he did when he gave up millions of dollars in a contract buyout with the Dallas Mavericks to join Miami this summer to play alongside superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo, who was acquired in a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks in June.

"That Heat culture is real," Thompson said. "I just love the intensity and competitiveness from everyone in this organization. Mr. Riley, Coach. My dad [Mychal Thompson] played for Mr. Riley [with the Lakers], so this is a pretty full-circle moment for us."

But this 4-6 Heat team has a long way to go before being considered great -- or maybe even playoff-bound.

Through 10 games, Miami has been outscored by 53 points. The Heat's defense has been downright putrid, ranking 25th in the league despite having several award-winning individual defenders.

Antetokounmpo is a former Defensive Player of the Year. Center Bam Adebayo has six All-Defensive team selections. Point guard Davion Mitchell's nickname is "Off Night" because of the suffocating pressure he applies on opposing ball handlers. Swingman Andrew Wiggins has been an elite perimeter defender at times during his career.

Through the first three weeks of the season, those individual accolades haven't translated.

"It can't just be on paper, and it can't just be reputation," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra said. "It has to be backed up by real actions."

When asked if the team simply needed time, Spoelstra scoffed.

"I don't know, but we don't want to use that as an excuse," he said. "The league's not waiting."

Antetokounmpo had a more specific assessment.

"Right now, we don't trust one another," he said after the loss to the Lakers. "We don't give that extra effort. We did it for two games, but we keep on having bad habits creep up in games."

articles.headline: Bobby Marks' NBA core danger tiers: 19 teams with major decisions looming
articles.description: With tax and apron penalties lurking everywhere, Bobby Marks examines 19 teams barreling toward core-altering decisions.
articles.body:
In the NBA's apron era, front offices need to be smarter than ever.

A failed win-now superstar trade not only depletes draft capital, it comes with the potential for severe roster-building penalties down the line. Repeated stalled playoff runs not only frustrate fan bases, they can create top-heavy teams that lack true avenues to improve. Recent NBA champions now seem to face immediate financial reckonings.

For the following 19 teams, roster-building dilemmas such as these are looming.

We put them into five tiers, ranging from franchises on the cusp of major decisions, to contenders desperate to prolong title windows, to teams whose futures hinge on their stars' next deal.

Tier 1: The danger zone

Milwaukee Bucks

Milwaukee is not in this tenuous position because of the aftermath of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade, but because of a roster move during the franchise's attempts at building another championship roster around him.

In July, the league opened a salary cap circumvention investigation into the Bucks and veteran guard Gary Trent Jr. The allegations stem from Trent signing a four-year, $64 million contract this summer despite averaging the second-fewest points and second-worst field goal percentage in his career.

Trent was coming off a two-year, $7.5 million contract with the Bucks, which paid him $3.7 million during the 2025-26 season and established his early Bird rights -- allowing Milwaukee to exceed the salary cap to re-sign him. So far this season, Trent has played a total of 13 minutes. (The league's collective bargaining agreement contains a clause against "prior agreement.")

If found guilty, Milwaukee could lose multiple first-round picks and face suspensions within its front office. The Bucks have no control of their next four first-round picks but do have five firsts (including two from Miami) starting in 2031.

New York Knicks

The defending champs are here despite the mandate from owner James Dolan to avoid the second apron altogether. The Knicks are projected to be $15 million below the threshold next season and will remain below even after filling their roster with minimum contracts. But, unless there is a trade to clear salary, New York will lose reserve guard Miles McBride.

Dolan's hardline approach won't truly be tested until the 2028 offseason.

Not including new contracts for Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart and a substantial raise for Jalen Brunson -- the guard's salary is expected to increase from $43 million to $66 million -- New York will be a projected $104 million under the second apron.

Towns has a $61 million player option for 2027-28, and there is a $22 million team option on Hart's deal. Both players remain extension eligible through June 30.

Oklahoma City Thunder
